title: task
description:
Purpose: Create TubeViz GitHub repo and migrate all code + Beads tracking

Prerequisites:
✅ GitHub CLI authenticated (ChrisLAS account)
✅ 3 local commits ready to push
✅ Beads tracking initialized and synced
✅ GPL v3 license allows forking

Execution Steps:

STEP 1: Create .gitignore entries (1 min)
---
Add test media files to .gitignore to keep repo lean:
- *.mp4 (test videos)
- *.flac (test audio) 
- *.jpg (test backgrounds)
- *.png (test thumbnails)
Exception: Keep .github/ assets and .beads/ tracking

Commands:
cat >> .gitignore << 'EOF'

# Test media files (keep repo lean)
*.mp4
*.flac  
*.jpg
*.png
# Exception: preserve .github/ assets
!.github/**/*.png
!.github/**/*.jpg
!.github/**/*.gif
EOF

git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: Ignore test media files"

STEP 2: Update README.md for TubeViz branding (3 min)
---
Changes needed:
- Replace "Jivefire" with "TubeViz"
- Update description to reflect enhanced features
- Add attribution to linuxmatters/jivefire
- Document vibeviz-inspired improvements
- Update build/usage examples

STEP 3: Create GitHub repository (1 min)
---
gh repo create ChrisLAS/TubeViz \
  --public \
  --description "Audio visualization tool for podcast/YouTube production - creates stunning frequency bar videos with Synthwave theming" \
  --clone=false

STEP 4: Configure new remote (1 min)
---
# Add TubeViz as new remote
git remote add tubeviz https://github.com/ChrisLAS/TubeViz.git

# Push all commits
git push -u tubeviz main

# Remove old origin
git remote remove origin

# Rename tubeviz to origin
git remote rename tubeviz origin

# Verify
git remote -v

STEP 5: Update Beads configuration (1 min)
---
Update .beads/config.yaml to reflect new repo

STEP 6: Final sync and push (1 min)
---
bd sync
git push

✅ TubeViz repo exists at github.com/ChrisLAS/TubeViz
✅ All code pushed successfully
✅ Beads tracking (.beads/ folder) included
✅ README updated with TubeViz branding
✅ git remote origin points to TubeViz
